newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds turn around early rise on T-bonds.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds turn around early rise on T-bonds.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished lower Tuesday as the market first followed U.S. Treasuries higher and subsequently fell with them in the afternoon.
Traders said, however, that trade picked up this session compared with the dull activity in recent days.
"The market more or less settled at the levels it opened," said a trader at a local bank.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.20 to 120.90, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 slipped 1/8 to 85-1/2.
The trader predicted that until Monday the market is likely to be extremely quiet considering the half day in the U.S. on Wednesday and the full holiday on Thursday.
Another trader predicted "there will be some profit-taking at these levels," before the market rises again next week.

He added that the increasing likelihood of a delay of the passage of the important labor reforms through the lower house of Congress "is not something the market is worried about, the labor reforms are already priced into the market."
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 6.60 percent from 6.65 percent.
